title: Shez rebuilds
summary: Shez begins rebuilding his broken people and establishes a righteous kingdom.

explicit_facts.text: Shez was a descendant of Heth, who had perished by famine with all his household except Shez.
Shez began to build up a broken people and built a righteous kingdom, remembering the Lord's bringing Jared and his brother across the deep.
Shez walked in the ways of the Lord and begat sons and daughters.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Shez can be shown overseeing rebuilding among the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The settlement's architecture, clothing, and landscape are not described.

narration.text: Shez began to build up again a broken people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The crossing of Jared and his brother is recalled, not narrated here as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the crossing as occurring in this scene.
Do not invent Heth's appearance or further details of the famine.

title: Shez, the eldest son, and a robber
summary: Shez, his father's eldest son, rebelled against him. A robber later smote Shez because of his exceeding riches, bringing peace again to his father.

explicit_facts.text: Shez was his father's eldest son and rebelled against him.
A robber smote Shez because of Shez's exceeding riches.
This brought peace again to Shez's father.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The robber may be shown striking Shez without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, appearances, and manner of the attack are unspecified.

narration.text: And his eldest son, whose name was Shez, did rebel against him; nevertheless, Shez was smitten by the hand of a robber, because of his exceeding riches, which brought peace again unto his father.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Shez here is the eldest son, not his father. The rebellion occurred before the attack and should not be combined with it in one visible moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the father as present at the attack.
Do not invent dialogue, a weapon, wounds, or a visible rebellion during the attack.
Do not portray the verse as explicitly saying Shez died.

title: Cities and succession
summary: The father builds cities as the people spread over the land; after his long life and death, Riplakish reigns.

explicit_facts.text: Shez's father built many cities; the people spread across the land; Shez lived to an exceedingly old age, begat Riplakish, died, and Riplakish reigned in his stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A city-building image can show people constructing settlements.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and design of cities and the specific timing of the succession are not visually detailed.

narration.text: Riplakish reigned in his stead.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse compresses events across Shez's life; do not portray them as simultaneous.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the father and son together at the moment of succession unless clearly separated in time.

title: Riplakish's burdens
summary: Riplakish imposes heavy taxes, builds spacious buildings and a beautiful throne, and imprisons people who cannot or will not pay.

explicit_facts.text: Riplakish had many wives and concubines, imposed grievous burdens and heavy taxes, and used the taxes to build spacious buildings.
He erected an exceedingly beautiful throne, built many prisons, and imprisoned those who would not or could not pay taxes.
Prisoners were made to labor continually for their support; those who refused to labor were put to death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A tax collection or prison setting may visualize the stated burdens.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Riplakish, his wives and concubines, buildings, throne, and prisons is unspecified.

narration.text: he did tax them with heavy taxes

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports multiple policies; avoid implying every detail happened at once.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a death or punishment not shown in the verse as happening in the chosen moment.
Do not invent personal identities for the people.

title: Work in prison
summary: Riplakish has fine gold refined and fine workmanship made in prison, while afflicting the people with his abominations.

explicit_facts.text: Riplakish had fine gold refined and all manner of fine workmanship wrought in prison.
He afflicted the people with his whoredoms and abominations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Prisoners may be shown laboring at metalwork.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific workmanship and the nature of the stated abominations are not described.

narration.text: he did cause to be wrought in prison

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not literalize or depict unspecified abominations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent what the abominations consisted of.

title: Rebellion against Riplakish
summary: After Riplakish has reigned for forty-two years, the people rebel; war returns, Riplakish is killed, and his descendants are driven out.

explicit_facts.text: After Riplakish reigned forty-two years, the people rose in rebellion and war began again; Riplakish was killed and his descendants were driven out of the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown rising in rebellion in a non-graphic conflict moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The battle, manner of Riplakish's death, and the descendants' identities are unspecified.

narration.text: the people did rise up in rebellion against him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse summarizes rebellion, war, death, and expulsion; this scene focuses on the rebellion.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show graphic injury or invent named rebels.

title: Morianton is anointed king
summary: After Morianton establishes himself king and eases the people's burden, the people anoint him to be their king.

explicit_facts.text: Morianton, a descendant of Riplakish, established himself king over all the land after many years of war.
After establishing himself king, Morianton eased the people's burden, gained their favor, and was anointed king by them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Depict the people's anointing of Morianton as one moment; do not show the earlier war or easing of burdens happening at the same time.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, participants' appearance, and method of anointing are unspecified.

narration.text: Morianton, (he being a descendant of Riplakish)
and did establish himself king over all the land.
he did ease the burden of the people
they did anoint him to be their king.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The anointing follows Morianton's establishment as king and his easing of the people's burden.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the war, easing of burdens, and anointing as simultaneous.
Do not invent an anointing ritual, dialogue, or named participants beyond Morianton.

title: Morianton's reign
summary: Morianton does justice to the people but not himself; he builds cities and the people become rich under his reign.

explicit_facts.text: Morianton did justice to the people but not to himself because of his many whoredoms, and was cut off from the presence of the Lord.
Morianton built many cities; the people became rich in buildings, gold, silver, grain, flocks, and herds.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A city and signs of material abundance can represent the prosperity described.
unspecified_visual_details: The text does not describe a visible manifestation of being cut off from the Lord.

narration.text: the people became exceedingly rich under his reign

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Being cut off from the presence of the Lord is a stated spiritual consequence, not a described visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine figure or supernatural action.

title: Kim takes the throne
summary: After Morianton's long life, Kim reigns in his stead for eight years and is not favored of the Lord because he does not reign righteously.

explicit_facts.text: Morianton lived to an exceedingly great age, begat Kim, and Kim reigned in his stead for eight years.
Kim did not reign in righteousness and was not favored of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Kim may be shown assuming the throne after Morianton's death.
unspecified_visual_details: No details of the transition or visible divine response are given.

narration.text: Kim did reign in the stead of his father

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse gives a succession and evaluation, not a visible divine appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent a specific unrighteous act.

title: Kim in captivity
summary: Kim's brother rebels and brings him into captivity, where Kim remains for life and begets children; in old age he begets Levi and dies.

explicit_facts.text: Kim's brother rebelled and brought Kim into captivity; Kim remained captive all his days and begat sons and daughters there.
In old age Kim begat Levi and died.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Kim may be shown as a captive; the verse supports captivity but not its physical conditions.
unspecified_visual_details: The brother's name, captivity setting, and appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: he did remain in captivity all his days

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse spans Kim's captivity and later life; do not merge all events into one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the identity of Kim's brother or details of the captivity.

title: Levi wins the kingdom
summary: Levi serves in captivity for forty-two years, makes war against the king of the land, and obtains the kingdom; he then does right in the Lord's sight and prospers.

explicit_facts.text: After his father's death, Levi served in captivity for forty-two years, made war against the king of the land, and obtained the kingdom.
After obtaining the kingdom, Levi did what was right in the Lord's sight; the people prospered, and Levi lived to old age and begat sons and daughters.
Levi begat Corom and anointed him king in his stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Levi may be shown fighting the king's forces in a non-graphic battle moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The king's identity and the battle's location and details are unspecified.

narration.text: he did obtain unto himself the kingdom.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The conflict and subsequent righteous reign are separate moments.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a name for the king or depict a divine appearance.

title: Corom and Kish
summary: Corom does good throughout his days and dies; Kish reigns after him and later dies, and Lib succeeds Kish.

explicit_facts.text: Corom did good in the Lord's sight all his days, begat many sons and daughters, and died; Kish reigned in his stead.
Kish also died, and Lib reigned in his stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A succession image may show Lib assuming rule after Kish.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance or details of the successions are stated.

narration.text: Kish reigned in his stead.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses span multiple reigns and deaths; do not portray them as simultaneous.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add circumstances for either death.

title: Lib hunts in the south
summary: During Lib's days the poisonous serpents are destroyed; people go south to hunt in a land covered with forest animals, and Lib becomes a great hunter. They build a great city by the narrow neck, preserve the south as wilderness, and the north is covered with inhabitants.

explicit_facts.text: Lib did good in the Lord's sight; in his days the poisonous serpents were destroyed.
People went into the land southward to hunt food because it was covered with animals of the forest; Lib became a great hunter.
They built a great city by the narrow neck of land where the sea divides the land.
They preserved the land southward as wilderness for game, and the land northward was covered with inhabitants.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A hunting scene may show Lib and people pursuing game in a forested southern region.
unspecified_visual_details: The serpent destruction is not described as an observed action; the city's design and geographic appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: Lib also himself became a great hunter.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses describe several developments, not one simultaneous moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent how the serpents were destroyed or depict that as a miracle.

title: Industry and trade
summary: The people work industriously, trade for gain, and mine and work many metals and fine workmanship.

explicit_facts.text: The people bought, sold, and trafficked with one another to get gain.
They worked many ores and metals, dug them from the earth, raised heaps of earth to obtain ore, and made fine work.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People may be shown trading goods and working metal.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific tools, goods, buildings, and clothing are unspecified.

narration.text: they did buy and sell and traffic one with another

prohibited_inventions: Do not add specific commodities or trade routes.

title: Crafts and tools
summary: The people make cloth, agricultural and animal-working tools, weapons of war, and finely crafted things.

explicit_facts.text: They had silks and fine-twined linen and made cloth to clothe themselves.
They made tools to plow, sow, reap, hoe, and thrash the earth.
They made tools to work their beasts.
They made weapons of war and works of exceedingly curious workmanship.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A craftwork moment may show people producing cloth or tools.
unspecified_visual_details: The tools, weapons, garments, and workmanship designs are not specified.

narration.text: they did make all manner of tools to till the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses list varied crafts; avoid implying all are made in a single workshop.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent distinctive weapons or designs.

title: A blessed land
summary: The people are described as exceedingly blessed and prosperous in a choice land.

explicit_facts.text: No people could be more blessed or prospered by the hand of the Lord; they were in a choice land, as the Lord had spoken.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A settled landscape may visually suggest prosperity, without implying a specific event.
unspecified_visual_details: The landscape and any visible sign of the Lord's hand are not described.

narration.text: they were in a land that was choice above all lands

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's hand and the choice land are statements of the source, not a described divine appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure or miracle.

title: Hearthom's captivity
summary: Lib begets sons, daughters, and Hearthom. Hearthom reigns after Lib; after twenty-four years, the kingdom is taken from him, and he spends the rest of his life in captivity. His descendants Heth, Aaron, Amnigaddah, and Coriantum also live in captivity; Coriantum begets Com.

explicit_facts.text: Lib lived many years and begat sons, daughters, and Hearthom.
Hearthom reigned in his father's stead. After twenty-four years, the kingdom was taken from him, and he spent the remainder of his life in captivity.
Hearthom begat Heth; Heth begat Aaron; Aaron begat Amnigaddah; Amnigaddah begat Coriantum; and Coriantum begat Com. Heth, Aaron, Amnigaddah, and Coriantum lived in captivity all their days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Hearthom may be shown alone in captivity after the loss of his kingdom.
unspecified_visual_details: The captors, location, clothing, and physical appearances are unspecified.

narration.text: And when Hearthom had reigned twenty and four years, behold, the kingdom was taken away from him.
And he served many years in captivity, yea, even all the remainder of his days.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The second narration excerpt refers to Hearthom. The passage then summarizes later generations rather than placing them all in one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the named generations together as contemporaries.
Do not invent captors, a location, or a specific means of confinement.

title: Com gains the kingdom
summary: Com draws away half the kingdom, reigns there for forty-two years, fights Amgid for many years, and gains power over the remainder.

explicit_facts.text: Com drew away half the kingdom and reigned over it for forty-two years.
Com fought the king Amgid for many years, gained power over him, and obtained power over the remainder of the kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A non-graphic battle moment may represent Com's war against Amgid.
unspecified_visual_details: The kingdom's division, battle location, and participants beyond the named leaders are unspecified.

narration.text: Com gained power over Amgid

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The separation of the kingdom and prolonged conflict are different stages.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or battle outcome details beyond those stated.

title: Robbers rise
summary: Robbers arise during Com's days, adopt ancient plans and oaths, and seek to destroy the kingdom. Com fights them but does not prevail.

explicit_facts.text: In Com's days robbers arose, adopted old plans, administered oaths after the manner of the ancients, and sought to destroy the kingdom.
Com fought against them much but did not prevail.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Robbers may be shown in conflict with Com's forces, without inventing identifying marks or biographies.
unspecified_visual_details: The robbers' organization, appearance, and the details of their oaths are unspecified.

narration.text: nevertheless, he did not prevail against them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The oaths are reported, not supplied as spoken dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the wording of oaths or depict a specific destruction of the kingdom.
